g.text: 13:30 wu, 12:44 cd 6:37, 6:39, 6:35, 6:29 w/2:20 rest (supposed to be 2:00) first time ever doing mile repeats! Kind of exciting...pleased w/the #s
Nice run through the Arboretum
Drove out to BC, ran Heartbreak hill (plus 5 others and a mofo)
3 laps around Briggs field, taking it real easy for tomorrow

1x1600 (400 rec), 4x300 (100 rec btw each, full rec after), 4x200 (walking rec): 6:07, 60, 60, 60, 60, 39, 37, 39, 37 Targets: 6:00, 61-63, 39-42 44 degress out or something like that! The cold really locked up my muscles I think, my stride felt off every time I tried to speed up and
shins were a bit un-warmed up

Don't like to overanalyze the last meet of the season but...I'll comment briefly: Not a bad race...time was poor but doesn't reflect much because of the conditions. (Windy, ~40 degrees, frozen ground, tough course) I think 82nd place is a pretty solid showing. I actually think I ran p
15 min wu,6x3 min, 4x30 sec, 1 min recovery btw all Swelling's almost down, pain way down, should be running by Sat.
it gets a bit windy on the esplanade... but that was a great run because it was right AFTER my 8.022 final! bu yah
1 min pickups every 10 min

1500 was solid, didn't make any moves really but didn't drag either. a bit wimpy/overconservative on the start, should have maintained contact splits: 84 (41/43), 85, 88, 64 800 - made up for my prior wimpyness, pleased w/the effort level splits: 37, 40, 42, 41

slow 800 wu (3:22), then 600-800-1000-800-600, 400 rest, 600 rest after the 1000. nearly right on: 2:15, 2:59, 3:43, 2:57, 2:11. didn't feel too hard but didn't feel like i could go much faster, either

Nancy took me to Fresh Pond, never been there before. Felt like crap starting out, didn't really want to be running, but by the time we were heading back it at least felt not hideous. Really gonna take down the miles this week and be fresh on Saturday
blood tests all came back normal
i love water, i love swimming, 16 days until San Diego! mixed it up, a few laps hard and such
should probably relax a bit more on the recovery runs
ran to and around the arboretum for a bit. a little heavy from being on a plane all night but it went. I wish I was home...

"2.5 mi continuous, run straights, jog turns" The object was to hit 25 for the 100 on laps 1-2, 23 for laps 3-4, 21 for 5-6, 20 for 7-8, and 18-20 for 9-10. Followed by a tempo 1200. Let's see if I can remember the actual times: 22, 22, 24, 22; 23, 21, 20, 22; mm... i dunno 19-21 for

ooh man that was fun! it was great to be able to go into a race "stupid" again. I didn't really know what I was doing, didn't care about splits, had never actually tried the water pit... and I just ran. It took me a long time to realize how well I did. Pretty much all day, actually. Q
developed a 101 fever during the day. My rule is not to run with a fever ever, so... geez what great timing for getting sick the first time all year

Hoooooooly sh*t! I don't know if there's any way to describe this race! It was so insanely hardcore, and SO MUCH FUN! Seriously, it was like, steeplchase times a hundred. In fact, there was a bit of steeplechasing involved, but it was more like steeple the way the horses do it... So t
felt really sluggish
visiting julie on cape cod... slept in and woke up just in time for lots of sun :-( Ran to woods hole and back
eh
home! felt surprisingly fresh, despite all the travelling. leaving for hawaii tomorrow, going to take a real easy week, maybe 5-6 mi/day

Brenna decided not to do the America's Finest City half marathon, so I took her number and ran it, just so I could have a more exciting long run this week. It was nice; I never like the road races because they're all on the road (imagine that) but the views were cool and it kept me fr

time includes a 15 min warmup on the turf. Felt awesome today! I expected to be slogging again, but everything was flowing and I wasn't tired. By my best estimate with Microsoft Streets and Trips, we ran just under 11.5 in 1:26:00. Even giving us a conservative estimate of 11.25, that

3xs "long loop" at Boston Commons. Workout was hard while I was doing it. Felt like I was struggling but also able to stay strong during the workout. In total it felt a little short, but I worked hard.

counting the continuous warmup and 6x100m strides for the extra 1.5. Don't have a race for three weeks; I'm looking forward to pounding out some solid workouts. Just need to keep my confidence up; like Carolyn said, I did the summer work, and I'm fit-- if nothing else, I'm at least ma

Hot damn! Finally, a good week of workouts. Today was huge, mentally if nothing else. Went to Franklin Park and did the course in 5x1000m segments, with 2:30 rest, plus Bear Cage Hill backwards once. Man, I really feel like I tore that one up. There were definitely those moments, but

I have never ellipticalled before. That's some lame-o stuff. Ran a mile on the track, afterwards, striding the straights. Had the trainers put a donut on my foot to keep the pressure off the lump, and it felt good. Planning to race Saturday.

Fenway track: 1x1600, 3x800, 1x300. Original workout called for 4x800, but I have a feeling HBH thinks we were working too hard because we went too fast. Anyway, the 800's were supposed to be tempo with the last 300 in a target of 63, I think. I ran: 6:13, 3:05 (65 300), 3:06 (63), 3:
easy run down the river, since i took monday off
ran longfellow-harvard with Mike and his friend from HS
Up Broken Hills, down including Guy Fleming. Didn't work especially hard, 12:30ish up the hill

Last run in Park City, went around 4:30 after a full day of boarding. I'm wiped; the little neighborhood hills were eating me alive and I didn't even have the energy to do my strength work. Showered and ate dinner after my run and then crashed for a nap at 7:30 p.m. Probably could hav
Gone boarding...
took the day off. with class 9-4 and a bunch of stuff to do in the evening, I just didn't have the energy to squeeze a workout in
taking it easy still. too bad continuous warmup killed me

sci-footbridge. reverse direction from last week's tempo, but did the same stretch of the esplanade. started w/kristen, but 5 min or so into the tempo her stomach started hurting and she told me to go on. Apparently she felt better soon after and spent the rest of the run trying to ca

did continuous warmup and steeple drills before running, wasn't done until 6:30. Everyone that had come in at that point said it was hailing pretty badly and pretty painful so I conceded and did laps around the indoor track. I'm ok with letting days like today be low mileage since we
TP state beach, north to Dahlia drive. Sun was out today, up in the 60's.... home is great.

meet got rained out, which was a disappointment, although I guess I would have been discouraged if I raced in crappy conditions and ran a bad time. The substitute workout was a team-wide relay race planned by HBH so the teams would be balanced. We ran a "DMR" and a "SMR", which were a
aquajog incl drills to breakup the boredom

Didn't really have my head in either race, so I don't regret the poor performances. Guess that's what happens when you develop a favorite event (and don't run it). The meet was non-scoring and I wasn't in any relays, I had a lot on my mind other than the race, plus it was raining, so

Jamaica Pond, around plus a little on the roads past the far end. started intending to run with everyone else, but I ran off as soon as we hit the river. Wasn't trying to run hard or fast or anything, but I just had a lot of restlesness in me and wanted to feel like I was moving. Juli
Did the workout on my own so that I wouldn't get competitive and overdo it. Just back and forth on the dirt/grass between BU and science museum.
ridiculously hot
nice and easy again today

tried to go with the guys at work again, but I was running late (actually working, ha) so I missed them. ran on my own and rolled my ankle a bit, but I was able to make it back ok. It didn't swell up but is sore now; I was taking tomorrow off anyway so it'll be ok

National Weather Service warned that the heat index would push 100 day, so I decided to wake up early and get the run out of the way. Definitely glad I did, it was already 77 when I got out the door at 5:30. longfellow-western, from wilg

wanted to make sure to take it easy so i left the watch at home. science museum-footbridge from WILG. while i was running past the longfellow bridge, some girl yelled out of the car, "hey speeeeedy!" it was really cute and made my day, I laughed out loud while running

decided to finally break it up into doubles to increase the quality of the runs, and partly so I wouldn't get bored. Probably should have done the easier run in the morning, since it seems that morning isn't my best hour, but oh well

grass loops again, only 7 this time. Ran w/Vicky, Gwen, Erika today, but was kind of dragging. The whole thing felt like it was too much effort--I led lap 3 but all the rest it was Erika and/or Vicky up front and I was just trying to prevent a gap. After looking at the splits though,

Footbridge/harvard with Gwen and Martha, with tape on the ankle. Didn't like the tape because I think it made me run a little funny, but if I focused I could do things normally. Could have maybe run a little faster but I was worried about Gwen's foot.
drove to the Arboretum and good some good hills in with Finn and Hana. A little bit sluggish but got through it.

drove out to Blue Hills Reservation with Jordan-- a long drive due to route choice and traffic, but worth it for variety's sake. We parked at Houghton's Pond, ran around there one, then crossed over to Ponkapoag Pond, where we wandered through the bog for a bit before making our way a
Off for Yom Kippur

The workout started with the Pizza Relay, a 3x1600 race (each runner doing one 1600). 10 minutes after the last finisher, we had to do the rest of our workout, 2x800 and 2x400 with 2:30 rest after the 8's and 75s rest between the 4's. I ran second leg, getting the baton a bit back fro

There's never any point in dwelling on the last meet of the season, but I'll just jot down a few quick reminders to myself for next year. I felt better when I woke up this morning and decided to race. I think from that moment on, I should have focused on removing any doubts on account

A dark, icy 5x5 min tempo. The rest between the first two went long trying to avoid the ice, but each of the intervals was about 10 s long too. Pretty poor conditions for a workout... for the first time in a while I felt pretty good and fresh, but I could never really open up because
Really slow today, lots of ice after yesterday's rain
Woke up early get a run in in Cambodia, before our 26-hour endeavour home, although I'm still having some stomach problems

I used a heat pad and the Stick and tried to run in the morning again, but it was too painful, and so after a mile and a half I finished up with 20 min on the elliptical. In the afternoon, though, after a heat and foam roll session, I had no problem running to Jamaica Pond with everyo
30 minutes of lap swimming and 30 minutes aquajogging.

We were trying to avoid crossing any brindges, so karen took me on a loop from Kendall Sq, to Broadway, to Harvard, and then back along the river via DeWolfe St. The GMaps Pedometer gives it as 5.75 . It was not a bad loop.

Finished class at 3 today and headed out toward the arboretum. Nice a sunny, a great day to get back into the long run habit, even if this one wasn't that long. A little sluggish from going faster yesterday, but no matter

fresh pond, back via harvard sq. Looks like the gmaps pedometer can save routes now, which is pretty cool. Here's where we went . Lauren, Karen, Adrienne and I were moving pretty well, but it felt good. I'm a bit sore from yesterday though

8x800, 200 rest, window 2:55-3:10. I was on my own for this one, Steph is cross training and Adrienne does 1500 workouts. But the 5k/10k group was doing 5x1600 at the same pace, essentially, so it worked out that I was able to start every other interval with them, and thus have someon
ran on the bike path that starts at the NTC. Unfortunately, all of our distance runs are going to happen here, and it's kind of a boring path. Just a paved road that pretty hilly and in the sun.
mm...warming up...yay....

3x800, 4x400, 4x200, rest was 200, 8:00, 100, 8:00, 100. The windows were 2:48-2:50; 80-82, and 35-37... I didn't realize until the warmup just how daunting 2:48-2:50 was, that's 4 seconds faster than last week's window, but I guess the workout was a lot shorter. Anyway, Karen and I p
started off real slow, I was tired from yesterday, but I got moving a bit. My knee is still a bit sore and the other leg got tired again, but I should be good tomorrow

Well the weather was bad, as they expected. A total of nearly 4" of rain for the day, temperatures around 50 degrees, although not as windy as expected. It really didn't get to me mentally, although it might have limited my warmup a bit. The times were kind of meaningless today, but I
First real day of work, so I ran from home at about 6pm. It stayed cloudy all day today though, so it was nice and cool. I have two new pairs of shoes now, to last me until winter probably.

Rancho Loop, modified for the new roads and whatnot, plus some detours. it was hot out today, and even though i didn't get out until 4:30 or so, I was still dripping and pretty thirsty by the end. It was also another hilly long run, probably more hills that last week, mostly because I

park loop plus High Bluff loop, with some detours for chinups. My legs have been getting progressively more beat up, but looking at my runs starting from Friday, it's not surprising. With the long weekend though, I wanted to use the extra time to put in some miles, so I'm not worried.

Got to the beach before 7:30am today to try to avoid some of the worst of the record-setting temperatures. It helped, especially having the sun low enough to have some shade, but I still definitely had to swing by 2 or 3 water fountains to grab a sip and douse my head and ponytail wit

pretty uninspired run today... not that I was particularly dragging or tired, but I just had nowhere really that I wanted to go. got home from work, sat around for a while, then just went out wandering.

morning run at lunch again. took a body fat test at the fitness center, and came in at 19.4%. I guess that's kind of high for a distance runner, but it's lower than I can ever remember, although I don't do it with any regularity. I know those things are super-inaccurate, but it's cool

got home at 12:30 and after sitting around, quasi-unpacking, I went for my real run around 2 pm. I started off feeling amazing, since I can actually breathe here, and headed toward the bike path for some relative flatness. Timed the first mile on the path at 7:45, and got to the end,

Jamaica Pond, the grass way. My group now is Rachel, Adrienne, Jacqui and Karen, but Karen was in the pool. We started off easy, but got moving a bit once we got past Longwood, trying to settle into the pace window. Adrienne and Jacqui dropped back at that point, and Rachel and I just
Franklin Park. Wandered around a bit then finished up with the course backwards. Finished up strong.
a decently paced run through Comm Ave and Beacon. Went a little longer than we intended, but it was ok since most of the group isn't racing tomorrow

Went on my own today, and made today's run a little longer since I didn't do a second morning run this week. felt good to go for a longer run, although I'm probably going to take tomorrow off just to give myself a reasonable shot this Saturday

Wilderness Pizza Relays. We were paired off with partners of equal ability, and each pair was handicapped so the fastest teams started last. We had to do four wilderness loops apiece for the race, then the top 8 added on two more. After some shuffling due to absentees, I ended up bein

ran out Mass Ave, turned on Columbus and followed the Southwest Corridor out until I hit 28 minutes. Wasn't moving very fast, definitely feeling yesterday a little. Ran exactly 8 min pace the whole way, based on the route I measured on GMaps.

Met up with Jessie to run, now that I'm back to campus. After a little snafu over where we were meeting which involved me crossing the Mass Ave bridge twice, we meet up and ran a JFK loop together. Today was a nice feeling run, I'm not sure how fast we were going but at least I wasn't

Got to practice late and was in a time crunch again to get back to lab, plus I was pretty wired from a midafternoon coffee, so when we got going it was Jessie and I moving pretty quickly. Felt good but I'm really starting to get worn out

ugh. being out of shape is no fun, especially at home where every run is hilly. After racing saturday, running up TP sunday, then trying to do a workout yesterday, my legs were fried. Oh, and also, I decided to lift in the morning before today's run, for some unknown reason. Yeah, I d

Parked at Fletcher Cove with the 'rents, but as usual ran on my own. Went North along the 101 to G Street in Encinitas. Nothing special, although I do love running by the campgrounds and smelling BBQ, surfwax and sunscreen. I also saw two twins, running, dressed in the same running ou
starting these up again, hopefully it will help

Ran around 8:00 this morning to get things out of the way so I could go to my robot competition tonight (yup, that's what the cool kids do). Wasn't really awake until the very end of the run and the whole thing was pretty lame and shuffle-y, a very slow run.

2 sets of 4x400: 81, 81, 80, 81, 82, 82, 83, 82. It's a big weird squeezing a workout between an "I just finished crying" warmup and an "I'm about to start crying again" cooldown, but that's what today was. I learned today that this jury is going to last through the middle/end of next

ugh, messiest run in a while. I ran alone earlier in the day so I could catch a flight to berkeley tonight, and I must have run in the absolute rainiest part of the day. It was a nice run until my foot got soaked in cold water, at which point I probably went progressivly slower and sl
Jamaica with Labuz, at an easy but steady pace. I love daylight saving's time!

same as last week, 8x800 with 2:30 rest, but faster windows: 2:53-3:00. It was super windy today and I was beat from standing all day yesterday, so I wasn't expecting much improvement from last week, but Adrienne and I ended up pretty much crushing the workout. I faded a little at the
easy run, then spent a lot of time on stretching, strides
Fresh Pond plus Sketchy Loop. Left my watch in the locker room but I'm pretty sure it was 11.5 or just over

charlestown with Liz, just us; we went early because i was supposed to have a dr. appt at 6. I didn't end up going because i saw the orthepedic guy earlier in the day, turns out I have two fractures, but both in the finger and both will heal fine.

2 sets of 4x400, 2:00 rest, 6:00 between sets. basically two-thirds of last week, windows of 78-82. This week though, was much easier (from the get-go, not just because it was shorter), and I felt great despite the dead legs from saturday. I mean, really, I was moving fast, even thoug

Well, came through in 6:04, pretty much the same as every race this season, then finished up in 11:39, pretty much the same as every race this season. Not much to say. Came through feeling strong at the start, as always, pushing the front of the unseeded heat with someone from Amherst
